focus.jbig: Records hold · scanner boarded 9 (mostly caveated) · NFP tomorrow
focus.jtag: Dow set another record, S&P held near 7,720, oil kept sliding on Iran-deal hopes — but NFP Friday and thin-volume boards keep it YELLOW
focus.jnote: The record-setting tape carried into Thursday, if a touch tired. Wednesday the Dow added ~263 points to a record ~54,349 while the S&P 500 slipped ~0.2% to ~7,723 — holding just under Tuesday's first-ever close above 7,700 — as oil kept sliding on optimism that a U.S.–Iran interim deal could reopen the Strait of Hormuz. The Nasdaq lagged (−0.8%) on an AMD/SpaceX-led chip wobble. This morning futures are mixed-to-firm, the VIX is low near 15.5–16.5, and gold is firm around $4,200. The catch: July payrolls (NFP) land Friday 8/7 with the 10-year still near a ~1.5-year high (~4.62%), and a huge Q2 earnings flood keeps single-name gap risk live — the scanner boarded 9 names this morning, but most Type A gaps confirmed on almost no volume with liquidity unverified on several. Validate every one at the open.
focus.notdown: The clean bullish gaps are CHYM and BEN. Chime (CHYM) reported a double beat and raised full-year revenue guidance to $2.73–2.75B, gapping ~9.6% — but relative volume was 0.15x pre-open (below the 1.3x bar) and there's only 1 S/R layer (the gap-floor) behind price. BEN is a clean Type C breakout that has HELD two sessions above its pivot with a 3-layer S/R stack and OK liquidity — the sturdiest name on the board. CSWC and ATI round out the bullish side, but ATI's options liquidity is UNVERIFIED. Confirm each gap holds and the chain is tradable at 9:35 before selling any bull put.
focus.notup: Z, ZETA, WRBY and PZZA are the boarded bearish gaps. Zillow (Z) gapped down ~10.6% after cutting its industry outlook and guiding full-year revenue below estimates despite an EPS beat — the cleanest bear-call story given the confirmed guidance cut and 3 S/R layers overhead. WRBY (OI just 13) and ZETA have UNVERIFIED liquidity. Selling bear calls into a record-setting, risk-on tape into NFP carries squeeze risk on any friendly headline — treat these as half-size-at-most and only if they fail the 9:35 validation on the downside.
focus.why: Why YELLOW, not GREEN? Composite is 38 (MILD) and P(≥1% gap) is ~30% (below the 35% trigger), which clears the numeric GREEN locks. But two things hold it at YELLOW: (1) NFP lands Friday 8/7 — a scheduled macro event inside 24h that alone forces at least YELLOW — with the 10Y still near a ~1.5-year high; and (2) nearly every boarded Type A name confirmed on near-zero relative volume (0.02–0.17x, all below the 1.3x bar) with several liquidity caveats (WRBY OI 13, ATI/ZETA/WRBY/URGN unverified). Half size, A-grade only, keep DTE short enough to clear NFP, and validate every candidate at 9:35 ET.

setups.read: Chime posted its second straight quarter of GAAP profitability and RAISED full-year revenue guidance to $2.73–2.75B, with the new Prime tier lifting ARPAM 6% to $260 — a clean double-beat that gapped the stock ~9.6% (~$28.40 vs $25.92). The severe EPS surprise plus the ≥5% gap earns A+. Caveats: relative volume 0.15x is well below the 1.3x bar, there's only 1 S/R layer (gap-floor $25.92, −8.7%) behind price, and note the CFO is stepping down effective Fri 8/7 — a small headline overhang.
setups.check_note: At 9:35 confirm price holds > $25.92 gap-floor AND > today's open, with volume building toward 1.3x. OI (1,500) and the $0.10 ATM spread pass on paper — still verify on the platform. Half size.

setups.read: Franklin Resources (BEN) is a clean ATH-region breakout that has HELD 2 sessions above its $34.44 pivot — sturdier than a same-day break — on breakout-day volume 1.61x the 50-day average. The best-structured name on the board; credit-sensitive asset managers caught a bid Wednesday, aligning with the tape.
setups.check_note: At 9:35 confirm price holds > the $34.44 pivot AND > today's open, upper third of range. Extension is modest (~1.6% above pivot) so there's room. Verify the ATM spread; half size on a NFP-eve tape.

setups.check_note: For a bear call, at 9:35 confirm price stays < $36.10 prior close AND < today's open, lower third of range. Watch for a relief bounce on any risk-on/Iran headline. Verify the $0.10 spread; half size.

risks: NFP · Fri 8/7 — July payrolls (consensus ~80k, prior 57k; unemployment ~4.2%) are the week's headliner and land inside 24h. A hot print pushes yields higher; a weak one boosts cut hopes — either way the single-biggest scheduled gap risk. Keep every spread's DTE clear of it.
10-year yield near a ~1.5-year high — the 10Y sits around 4.62% with the Fed hawkish. Any further rate pop pressures long-duration tech even on a risk-on tape, and stacks on top of the jobs number.

Earnings-cluster gap risk — 9 names boarded today; COP, Airbnb, Cloudflare, Lyft and Warner Bros. Discovery report today. Nearly every boarded Type A gap confirmed on near-zero volume — confirm each chain is real and tradable at 9:35 before selling anything.

Thin-liquidity boarded names — WRBY (OI 13), URGN (117), ATI (428) are below/near the 500-OI bar; ATI, ZETA, WRBY and URGN all show liquidity UNVERIFIED. Several may be untradeable in practice — do not force a fill.

Iran / Hormuz talks — an interim deal (Iran-Oman shipping route) could land soon, but nothing is signed. A breakdown or any Strait disruption sends crude and the whole tape gapping — the week's biggest wildcard.
